issues.description: The problem statement (UML) declares Pneumatic.raisePressure(int) with return type void, but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares raisePressure(int) returning boolean. Moreover, the solution's implementing classes (LaunchedRollerCoaster and LaunchedDropdownTower) provide overrides with a void return type, which conflicts with the solution interface's boolean return type and would cause a compilation error. This mismatch between the UML/specification and the solution (and an internal inconsistency in the solution itself) will confuse students about the correct signature to implement and prevents a working implementation.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the raisePressure signature across all artifacts. The UML/problem statement specifies void, and the implementations in the solution already use void, so update the Pneumatic interface to declare: void raisePressure(int pressureIncrease); (and ensure the template Pneumatic.java includes the same signature). Alternatively, if the intended return type is boolean, update the UML/problem statement and the implementing classes to return boolean and implement/return appropriate values — but prefer making the interface void to match the UML and current implementations.
